Horayot 4a:10.english: Ḥizkiyya said that the verse states: “And they performed one of all the mitzvot” (Leviticus 4:13), from which it is inferred that one is liable for nullification for a portion of all the mitzvot and not for nullification of all the mitzvot. The Gemara asks: The term mitzvot is plural, which indicates at least two. If that is the source, there should be liability even if the judges issue a ruling abolishing the entire essence of one mitzva, as one mitzva is a portion of two mitzvot. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Although the word is vocalized in the plural, as mitzvot, the word mitzvat is written, without a second vav, as though it were in the singular.

Horayot 4a:11.english: Rav Ashi said: The tanna derives a verbal analogy, learning the meaning of the term “matter” written in the context of the erroneous ruling from the term “matter” written in the context of the rebellious elder. As it is written with regard to the rebellious elder: “If there shall be a matter [davar] too hard for you…You shall not turn aside from the matter [haddavar] that they shall declare unto you, to the right nor to the left” (Deuteronomy 17:8–11). Just as one becomes a rebellious elder only when the rebellious elder's dispute with the Sages is with regard to a portion of the matter and not an entire matter, so too, with regard to an erroneous ruling of the court, the court's error must be with regard to a portion of the matter and not the entire essence of the matter.

Horayot 4a:4.english: The Gemara references the Mishnaic discussion (Horayot 3b:12) where ben Azzai said to Rabbi Akiva: In what way is this person who went overseas different from one who sits in his house? The Gemara asks: Rabbi Akiva said well to ben Azzai. How did a scholar of ben Azzai's caliber fail to understand that distinction?

Horayot 4a:6.english: The mishna teaches: In a case where the judges of the court issued an erroneous ruling to abolish the entire essence of the mitzva, that is not a valid ruling, and the court is exempt from bringing an offering. The Sages taught: The verse states: “And the matter is hidden from the eyes of the congregation” (Leviticus 4:13), from which it is derived that there is liability only when a single matter is hidden but not in a case where the judges will abolish the entire mitzva. How so? If the court said: There is no prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a menstruating woman written in the Torah, or there is no prohibition against performing prohibited labor on Shabbat written in the Torah, or there is no prohibition against engaging in idol worship written in the Torah, one might have thought that the judges would be liable. Therefore, the verse states: “And the matter is hidden,” and not that the entire mitzva will be hidden. Accordingly, if the judges issued that ruling, the judges are exempt from bringing an offering.

Horayot 4a:7.english: But if the judges said: There is a prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a menstruating woman written in the Torah, but one who engages in intercourse with a woman who observes a clean day for a day she experiences a discharge is exempt; or if they said: There is a prohibition against performing prohibited labor on Shabbat written in the Torah, but one who carries out objects from the private domain to the public domain is exempt; or if they said: There is a prohibition against engaging in idol worship written in the Torah, but one who bows to the idol but did not sacrifice an offering is exempt, one might have thought that the judges would be exempt. Therefore, the verse states: “And the matter is hidden,” from which it is derived that there is liability only for a matter, a single detail, but not for the entire essence. In this case, since the judges ruled to abolish only a detail of the mitzva, the court is liable.

Horayot 4a:8.english: The Gemara analyzes the latter clause of the baraita. The Master said: One might have thought that the judges would be exempt. The Gemara asks: But if in a case of sustaining a portion of the mitzva and nullifying a portion of the mitzva the judges are exempt, and in a case of abolishing the entire essence of the mitzva the judges are exempt, as explained in the first clause of the baraita, in what case would the court be liable? The Gemara answers: This is what is difficult for the tanna: Say that the term “matter” is referring to the entire matter, and the court is liable even if the judges ruled to abolish the entire mitzva. Therefore, the verse states: “And the matter is hidden [venelam davar].”

Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:1.hebrew: חזקיה אמר: מסיפא דקרא נפקא, מכל מצוות דמשמע מכל מצוות של שבת דהוי ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת; או מכל מצוות של עבודת כוכבים דהוי ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת; או מכל מצוות נדה דהוי ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת, ולא כל מצוות השבת דהוי עוקר כל הגוף, ולא כל מצוות דנדה ודעבודת כוכבים דעוקר כל הגוף:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:1.english: Ḥizkiyya said: It is derived from the end of the verse, "of all the *mitzvot*," which implies of all the *mitzvot* of Shabbat, which is nullifying a portion and sustaining a portion; or of all the *mitzvot* of idol worship, which is nullifying a portion and sustaining a portion; or of all the *mitzvot* of a menstruating woman, which is nullifying a portion and sustaining a portion, and not all the *mitzvot* of Shabbat, which is abolishing the entire essence, and not all the *mitzvot* of a menstruating woman and idol worship, which is abolishing the entire essence:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:2.hebrew: מצות תרתי משמע: כלומר מצוות טובא משמע, כגון נדה, שבת, ועבודת כוכבים, דהכי משמע: ועשה אחת מכל מצוות ה' דעבד חד מהני: או שבת, או עבודת כוכבים, או נדה, ולעולם בעוקר כל הגוף קא מיירי:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:2.english: *Mitzvot* indicates two: That is to say, *mitzvot* implies many, such as a menstruating woman, Shabbat, and idol worship, for this is what is inferred: "and performed one of all the *mitzvot* of the Lord," that he performed one of these: either Shabbat, or idol worship, or a menstruating woman, and it is always dealing with abolishing the entire essence:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:3.hebrew: אמר ר"נ בר יצחק מצות כתיב: בחד וי"ו דחדא מצוה משמע, דהכי משמע: ועשה אחת מכל מצוות דשבת, או אחת מכל מצוות דעבודת כוכבים, או אחת מכל מצוות דנדה, דהוי מקיים מקצת דשבת ומבטל מקצת; והוא הדין לעבודת כוכבים, והוא הדין לנדה, והוא הדין לשאר מצוות, דקיום מקצת וביטול מקצת חייב, ועוקר כל הגוף פטור:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:10:3.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: *Mitzvat* is written: With one vav, which implies one *mitzva*, for this is what is inferred: "and performed one of all the *mitzvot* of Shabbat," or "one of all the *mitzvot* of idol worship," or "one of all the *mitzvot* of a menstruating woman," which is sustaining a portion of Shabbat and nullifying a portion; and the same applies to idol worship, and the same applies to a menstruating woman, and the same applies to other *mitzvot*, that for sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion one is liable, and for abolishing the entire essence one is exempt:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:11:1.hebrew: מה זקן ממרא מן הדבר ולא כל דבר: דהא כתיב מן הדבר. ותנן באלו הן הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פח:): האומר אין תפלין לעבור על דברי תורה פטור, חמש טוטפות להוסיף על דברי סופרים חייב, דהיינו מן הדבר ולא כל דבר:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:11:1.english: Just as a rebellious elder is only for part of the matter and not the entire matter: For it is written "from the matter." And we learned in "Eilu Hen HaNikhnakin" (Sanhedrin 88b): One who says there are no *tefillin* to transgress the words of the Torah is exempt; five *totafot* to add to the words of the Scribes is liable. That is part of the matter and not the entire matter:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:12:1.hebrew: אין בית דין חייבין - דלא הוי הוראה מעליא עד שיורו להתיר בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין שיהא אסור, שהורו להיתר בדבר איסור שאין כתוב בתורה בהדיא:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:12:1.english: A court is not liable - because it is not a proper ruling until they rule to permit something that the Sadducees do not agree is forbidden, meaning they ruled to permit something forbidden that is not explicitly written in the Torah.

Rashi on Horayot 4a:12:2.hebrew: זיל קרי בי רב הוא - דכיון דאפשר לו ללמוד ולידע, לא הוי שוגג מעליא וקרוב למזיד הוי:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:12:2.english: Go learn in a children’s school - because since it is possible for him to learn and know, it is not a proper error, but rather close to an intentional transgression.

Rashi on Horayot 4a:13:1.hebrew: אחד לאחד: היינו יום כנגד יום:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:13:1.english: One for one: This is "a day for a day".

Rashi on Horayot 4a:15:1.hebrew: דאמרי כדרכה אסירא: גמר ביאה ושלא כדרכה שריא:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:15:1.english: That they said: In the typical manner is forbidden: completion of intercourse, and in an atypical manner is permitted:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:15:2.hebrew: והא: שלא כדרכה נמי כתיב משכבי אשה: שני משכבות: אחד כדרכה ואחד שלא כדרכה:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:15:2.english: And is it not: In an atypical manner too, it is written "manners in which one lies with a woman": two manners of lying: one in the typical manner and one in an atypical manner:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:16:1.hebrew: דאמרי כדרכה אסירא אפי' העראה: דהאי דכתיב את מקורה הערה בכדרכה:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:16:1.english: That they said: In the typical manner is forbidden even initial penetration: For that which is written "he has uncovered her fount" refers to the typical manner:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:16:2.hebrew: אי הכי: מאי איריא דקתני שהורו בשומרת יום כנגד יום? אפילו נדה נמי בכי האי גוונא קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת הוא, והוי בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:16:2.english: If so: Why specifically does it teach that they ruled regarding a woman who observes a day for a day? Even a menstruating woman too, in such a case, it is sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion, and it would be a matter about which the Sadducees do not agree:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:17:1.hebrew: אלא לעולם בכדרכה: דאמרי בשומרת יום העראה שריא אפילו בכדרכה, וגמר ביאה הוא דאסיר. ודקאמרת הא העראה כתיב, דאמרי: העראה באשה נדה הוא דכתיב, ולא בשומרת יום. הלכך לא מתוקמא בנדה אלא בשומרת יום, והוי בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בה:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:17:1.english: Rather, always in the typical manner: That they said regarding a woman who observes a day, initial penetration is permitted even in the typical manner, and completion of intercourse is forbidden. And what you said, "is not initial penetration written," they said: initial penetration is written regarding an afflicted woman (a menstruating woman during her period) and not regarding a woman who observes a day. Therefore, it is not established regarding a menstruating woman, but regarding a woman who observes a day, and it is a ruling about which the Sadducees do not agree:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:17:2.hebrew: ואי בעית אימא: דקאמרת שומרת יום הא כתיבא, הא לא קשיא. דכי קתני כגון דאמרי: זבה לא הוה אלא היכא דחזיא ביממא, כדכתיב כל ימי זובה. אבל היכא דחזיא בליליא, טהורה. והוא הדין לשומרת יום דאמרי דהוא היכא דקחזיא ביממא, דהיינו בימי זיבה. הלכך לא מתוקמא בנדה אלא בשומרת יום ובזבה, והויא הוראה בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:17:2.english: And if you wish, say: What you said, "a woman who observes a day is written," this is not difficult. For when it teaches, for example, that they said: a *zava* is only where she sees during the day, as it is written "all the days of her discharge." But where she sees at night, she is pure. And the same applies to a woman who observes a day, that they said it is where she sees during the day, which means during the days of *ziva*. Therefore, it is not established regarding a menstruating woman, but regarding a woman who observes a day and a *zava*, and it is a ruling about which the Sadducees do not agree:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:19:1.english: Passing or throwing: Are not explicitly written:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:21:1.hebrew: השתחואה שלא כדרכה: כגון משתחוה לפעור או למרקוליס:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:21:1.english: Bowing in an atypical manner: For example, bowing to Pe'or or to Mercurius:

Rashi on Horayot 4a:21:2.hebrew: השתחואה: בפשוט ידים ורגלים, כדכתיב (בראשית י״ט:א׳): וישתחו אפים ארצה:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:21:2.english: Bowing: With outstretched hands and feet, as it is written (Genesis 19:1): "and bowed down with their faces to the ground":

Rashi on Horayot 4a:5:1.english: Set out on the way - to go overseas, but he is still in the city.

Rashi on Horayot 4a:5:2.english: There is a practical difference between them - According to Rabbi Akiva, he is exempt, as he set out on the way. Since he is preoccupied, it would not have been possible for him to hear that they (the court) reversed their ruling. Therefore, he relies on the court and is completely exempt.

Rashi on Horayot 4a:8:1.hebrew: תנא הכי קשיא ליה דבר כולה מלתא משמע: דהורו לעקור כל הגוף, דהא לא כתיב מדבר. ואימא איפכא: דהורו לבטל במקצת ולקיים במקצת יכול יהו פטורין, וכי הורו לעקור כל הגוף יהו חייבין?
Rashi on Horayot 4a:8:1.english: The Tanna, this is what was difficult for him: 'matter' implies the entire thing, that they ruled to abolish the entire essence, for it is not written 'from a matter'. And say the opposite: that they ruled to nullify a portion and sustain a portion, they might be exempt, and when they ruled to abolish the entire essence, would they be liable?

Rashi on Horayot 4a:8:2.hebrew: ת"ל ונעלם דבר: בא ללמד דבטול מקצת וקיום מקצת חייב:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:8:2.english: The verse states: "And the matter is hidden": It comes to teach that for nullifying a portion and sustaining a portion, one is liable.

Rashi on Horayot 4a:9:1.hebrew: מאי משמע: כלומר היכי משמע האי ונעלם דהוי קיום מקצת ובטול מקצת:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:9:1.english: What is inferred?: That is to say, how is this "venelam" inferred to be sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion?

Rashi on Horayot 4a:9:2.hebrew: אמר עולא קרי ביה ונעלם מדבר: דהאי מ"ם דנעלם שדיא אדבר, דמ"ם נדרשת לפניו ולאחריו, וקרי ביה ונעלם מדבר דמשמע מדבר ולא כל דבר:
Rashi on Horayot 4a:9:2.english: Ulla said: Read into it as "venelam middavar": For the letter mem of "venelam" applies to both here and there, and a mem is expounded before it and after it, and read into it "venelam middavar," which means "from a matter" and not "the entire matter".

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4a:4.english: And this answer is so simple, that it is puzzling that ben Azzai would ask a question whose answer is clear. And for this reason, Rava explains that ben Azzai surely did not come to ask about one who is already overseas, but rather he understood from Rabbi Akiva's words that the expression "went overseas" means one who is about to go there, who is on his way there and is not yet there.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4a:5.english: Because he is preoccupied with preparations for his journey, he does not hear the new developments each day. And some have asked: If it is due to preoccupation, why specifically for one going overseas? Why do we not also worry about one going to another city? And it was answered in one way that there is a distinction between the preoccupation of a short journey and that of a long journey. And furthermore, it can be said that what is stated as 'overseas' is not literal, but rather refers to anyone embarking on a long journey who is preoccupied with his affairs, and therefore does not know what is new (Magen Giborim).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4a:12.english: And this is not an erroneous ruling, but rather a simple mistake. Or it is a matter of intentional transgression (and see Rashi and Meiri and others).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4a:17.english: And if she saw blood at night, she is not impure (Rashi). Or, one who sees during the day has the status of a zava, and at night she is like a niddah (Rach).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4a:19.english: But if the court erred in a matter that is not explicitly stated in the Torah and is not the uprooting of the entire essence, then they bring an offering, and all those who performed the transgression are exempt from individual sin-offerings. For example, if they said that there is a prohibition against carrying out on Shabbat but not the law of passing, or if they permitted bowing to an idol when it does not involve extending hands and feet. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 14:2).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4a:5.english: One who was about to embark to countries overseas and performed a transgression on the basis of the ruling of the court that circulated throughout a majority of the public, even if he did so after the court reversed its ruling, is exempt from bringing an individual sin-offering, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva (Rambam Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 14:5).

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:10.english: Ḥizkiyya said, the verse states: [the verse]: "And they performed one of all the *mitzvot*" (Leviticus 4:13), "of all the *mitzvot*" — and not all the *mitzvot*. And they wonder: "*Mitzvot*" at least two [two] is inferred, if so, they would not bring an offering until they err in one of the many *mitzvot* and abolish it completely! Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: "*Mitzvat*" is written [written] with one vav, and we read it as "*mitzvat*" lacking a vav.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:11.english: Rav Ashi said: He derives [he learned] a verbal analogy "matter" "matter" from the rebellious elder, as it is written about him [that it is said about him] regarding the rebellious elder: "If there shall be a matter too hard for you... You shall not turn aside from the matter that they shall declare unto you, to the right nor to the left" (Deuteronomy 17:11), just as the rebellious elder is only when he disputes the Sages concerning a matter that is part of the matter and not the entire matter, so too, regarding a ruling in which they erred, it is a matter and not the entire essence.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:12.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says: A court is not liable to bring an offering unless it issues an erroneous ruling concerning a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree. For the Sadducees do not accept the Oral Torah, but rather understand the verse as it is written. That is to say, they err in a matter that is not explicitly stated in the Torah, or does not simply derive from the verses. But with regard to a matter with which even the Sadducees agree, they are exempt. What is the reasoning for this exemption? It is a topic that you could go learn in a children’s school. That is to say, this matter is so simple that even children in a children's school know it, and if a court erred in this, it is not considered an error of the court.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:13.english: We learned in the mishna: When are they liable? When they erred and said: There is a prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a menstruating woman written in the Torah, but one who engages in intercourse with a woman who observes a clean day for a day she experiences a discharge is exempt. And it is difficult according to Shmuel's words: And why are they liable for this? The halakha of a woman who observes a day for a day is written in the Torah regarding a niddah not in her menstrual period: “And she shall count for herself” (Leviticus 15:28); this teaches that she counts one clean day for one day (observes a day for a day). If so, the matter is stated in the written Torah, and even the Sadducees agree to it!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:14.english: And they answer: They did not err in the actual law of a woman who observes a day for a day, but rather they said: Ha'ara'ah (the initial stage of intercourse) is permitted with a menstruating woman; it is the completion of intercourse that is forbidden. And they ask: This is also written: “He has uncovered her fount” (Leviticus 20:18), which explicitly states the prohibition of ha'ara'ah with a menstruating woman!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:15.english: And they answer: They said: If one engages in intercourse with her in the typical manner - it is forbidden; if in an atypical manner (anal intercourse) - it is permitted. And they ask: But it is written: “The manners in which one lies with a woman” (Leviticus 18:22), and from here it simply emerges that there are two manners of lying with a woman, in the typical manner and in an atypical manner, and this is as if it is explicitly written!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:16.english: And they answer: They say thus: In the typical manner - even ha'ara'ah is forbidden. In an atypical manner - it is the completion of intercourse that is forbidden, but ha'ara'ah is permitted. And they ask: If so, even a niddah herself during her menstrual period would also be permitted, and they would say that only the completion of intercourse is forbidden. So why does the mishna state that they erred concerning a woman who observes a day for a day!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:17.english: Rather, actually, it is concerning ha'ara'ah in the typical manner, and they say: Ha'ara'ah with an afflicted woman (see there, 18), a niddah during her menstrual period, is what is written, and not concerning a woman who observes a day for a day. And if you wish, say instead that they say: A woman assumes the status of a zava (who discharges blood from her source, not during her menstrual period) is only during the day and not at night, as it is written: “All the days of her discharge” (Leviticus 15:26).

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:18.english: And immediately they ask: We learned in the mishna: There is a prohibition against performing prohibited labor on Shabbat written in the Torah, but one who carries out objects from one domain to another is exempt. And they ask: According to Shmuel, and why are they liable? With regard to carrying out, isn’t it written: “Neither carry a burden out of your houses” (Jeremiah 17:22), and the Sadducees agree to it!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:19.english: And they answer: They say: Carrying out is what is forbidden, but carrying in from the public domain to the private domain is permitted. And if you wish, say instead that they say: Carrying out is what is forbidden, but passing or throwing from one domain to another is permitted.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:20.english: And furthermore, we learned in the mishna: There is a prohibition against engaging in idol worship written in the Torah, but one who bows to the idol is exempt. And why should they be liable? Is not one who bows explicitly written, as it is written: “You shall not bow to another god” (Exodus 34:14)!

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:21.english: And they answer: They say: When bowing is forbidden, it is in its typical manner, when this is the way of worship for this idol. But in an atypical manner, where one does not bow to it, it is permitted. And if you wish, say instead that they say: Bowing itself, it is in its typical manner that it is forbidden. And when is that? When it involves the extension of hands and feet, which is a complete bowing like in the Temple. But bowing that does not involve the extension of hands and feet is permitted.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:4.english: We learned in the Mishna: Ben Azzai said to him: In what way is this different from one who sits in his house? And Rabbi Akiva answered him that one who goes overseas has no possibility to hear. And they ask: Rabbi Akiva said well to ben Azzai in explaining the difference, and how did a great sage like ben Azzai not understand this?

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:5.english: Rava said: Here we are not talking about one who has already gone overseas, but rather one who set out on the way, who has not yet left overseas, but is preoccupied with preparations for departure. And in this matter there is a practical difference between them. According to ben Azzai, he is liable — as he is in his home and there is no difference between him and one who sits in his home. According to Rabbi Akiva, he is exempt — as he has set out on the way and is considered as one who has left.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:6.english: We learned in the mishna that if the court ruled to abolish the entire essence, this is not a ruling, and the court is exempt. And regarding this, the Sages taught: [the Sages taught]: "And the matter is hidden from the eyes of the congregation" (Leviticus 4:13) — and not that the entire mitzva should be abolished. How so? They said: There is no menstruating woman in the Torah, or they said: There is no Shabbat in the Torah, and similarly if they said: There is no idol worship in the Torah, would they be liable? The verse states: "And the matter is hidden," and not that the entire mitzva will be hidden, and if they ruled thus by mistake — they are exempt.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:7.english: But they said: There is a menstruating woman in the Torah, but one who has intercourse with a woman who observes a day for a day is exempt, or they said: There is Shabbat in the Torah, but one who carries out from the private domain to the public domain is exempt, and similarly if they said: There is idol worship in the Torah, but one who bows to it is exempt, would they be exempt? The verse states: "And the matter is hidden" and not the entire essence.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:8.english: And they clarify: The Master said: [the Sage]: They might be exempt. And they wonder: And if [and if] in sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion they are exempt, and in abolishing the entire essence we already said that they are exempt, in what [in what] are they liable? And they answer: This is what was difficult for the tanna: [this was difficult for him], say: [say]: "matter" means the entire thing: [the entire thing means]! that the essence of an entire mitzva was hidden, the verse states: "And the matter is hidden."

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4a:9.english: And they ask: What is inferred? [What is the meaning?] How does what he wanted to prove derive from here! Ulla said: Read into it [read in it] as if there was a double 'mem' "venelam middavar." Part of the matter, and not all of it.

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:11:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר יליף דבר דבר מזקן ממרא: והתם יליף בתוספתא בין דם לדם ולא כל דבר. והני דהכא לא שמיע להו ברייתא דילן מטעמא אחרינא:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:11:1.english: Rav Ashi said: He derives "matter" "matter" from the rebellious elder: And there it is derived in the Tosefta from "between blood and blood" and not the entire matter. And these here did not hear our *baraita* for another reason:

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:12:1.hebrew: בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו - והא דאצטריך למעוטי כוליה דבר ולא נפיק משום דצדוקין מודין בו. כמו בתו מאנוסתו דלית להו גזירה שווה, או אם חמיו ואם חמותו. ומתניתין דנקט נדה ושבת ועבודת כוכבים לא משום דאהנהו דוקא קאי, אלא רק לפרש קיום מקצת נקטינהו:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:12:1.english: Concerning a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree - And this is what was necessary to exclude the entire matter, and it does not emerge because the Sadducees agree to it. Like his daughter from a raped woman, for whom they do not have a verbal analogy, or his father-in-law and mother-in-law. And the mishna that mentions Niddah, Shabbat, and idolatry is not because it refers specifically to them, but only to explain the fulfillment of a partial mitzva.

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:13:1.hebrew: יש נדה אבל הבא על שומרת יום כו': בנדה גופה הוי מצי לאשכוחי טובא, כגון בדם אדום, בדם שחור, וטובא דחשיב בתורת כהנים. אלא דאתי לאשמועינן אפילו בשומרת יום, ובנדה מקרי קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת. ובגמרא דפריך אי הכי אפילו נדה נמי, הכי פירושו: אפילו נדה בכי האי גוונא אי הוה בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו, הוי קיום מקצת:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:13:1.english: There is a menstruating woman but one who has intercourse with a woman who observes a day, etc.: Regarding a menstruating woman herself, one could find many examples, such as red blood, black blood, and many that are listed in Torat Kohanim. But it comes to teach us even regarding a woman who observes a day, and regarding a menstruating woman, it is considered sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion. And in the Gemara, which asks "if so, even a menstruating woman too," this is its explanation: even a menstruating woman in such a case, if it was a matter about which the Sadducees do not agree, it would be sustaining a portion:

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:13:2.hebrew: הכתיב וספרה לה לא גרסינן; דהא בשמעתא בתרייתא דנדה מפיק לה ממשכב נדתה יהיה לה:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:13:2.english: It is written "and she shall count for herself": We do not read this, for in the last *shma'ata* of Niddah, it is derived from "as the lying of her impurity shall be for her".

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:15:1.hebrew: שלא כדרכה נמי הכתיב כו': משמע דצדוקין מודין בו. ובפרק אחד דיני ממונות גבי טעה בנואף ונואפת, משמע דאין צדוקין מודין בו התם בהעראה שלא כדרכה:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:15:1.english: Also in an atypical manner, is it not written, etc.: It implies that the Sadducees agree to it. And in the chapter "Echad Dinei Mamonot" regarding one who erred with an adulterer and adulteress, it implies that the Sadducees do not agree to it there regarding initial penetration in an atypical manner:

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:17:1.hebrew: הכתיב כל ימי זובה: הני מילי לאתויי קרא קמא דכתיב זוב דמה ימים רבים:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:17:1.english: It is written "all the days of her discharge": These words come to include the first verse, where it is written "the flow of her blood for many days":

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:19:1.hebrew: דאמרי הוצאה אסירא והכנסה שריא: ותנא הוצאה הכנסה קרי לה, כדאמרינן במסכת שבת (ב:) ובמסכת שבועות (ה.):
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:19:1.english: That they said: Carrying out is forbidden and carrying in is permitted: And the Tanna calls carrying out "carrying in," as we say in Tractate Shabbat (2b) and in Tractate Shevuot (5a):

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:19:2.hebrew: איכא דאמרי: הוצאה והכנסה (שריא) [הוא דאסירא], אף על גב דהכנסה לא כתיבא, סברא היא: מה לי אפוקי, מה לי עיולי (שבת צו:):
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:19:2.english: Some say: Carrying out and carrying in (is permitted) [is forbidden]: Even though carrying in is not written, it is a logical inference: What is the difference to me to take out, what is the difference to me to bring in (Shabbat 96b):

Tosafot on Horayot 4a:9:1.hebrew: קרי ביה ונעלם מדבר: דמ"ם מונעלם קאי להכא ולהכא; ואמר בירושלמי דאיכא דאמר: גורעין ודורשין מתחלת פרשה לסופה, ואידך אף באמצע פרשה: ויצקת עליה שמן, הצקת שמן המנחה, ללמד כל המנחות ליציקה. הקשה ריב"ק בר' מאיר: מאי שנא דהכא דרשינן ונעלם מדבר, וגבי עדות יקום דבר לכ"ע דרשינן דבר ולא חצי דבר. ויש לומר דודאי דבר כולה דבר משמע, והכא מעניינו דקרא: מכדי כתיב אחת מכל מצוות ה' דמשמע מצוה שלימה, למאי הלכתא כתב דבר? אלא על כרחך למדרש ונעלם מדבר אפילו דבר אחד מן המצוות. וכן בכל דוכתי גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין משום דוחקא דקרא דאיהו דחיק ומוקים אנפשיה. כי ההוא דהזהב דהוה ליה למכתב וחמישיתו יוסף עליו, כי היכי דכתיב גבי מעשר. ובפרק יש נוחלין הוה ליה למכתב אשתו תירש את הנחלה, וכי כתב קרא, צריך ליישב המקרא על ידי גרעון ותוספת. תימה: מנא לן דאתי קרא לחייב רק קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת? דלמא קרא אתא אפילו לחייב בכך, וכל שכן בביטול כל הגוף, כדאמר בפרק הנחנקין גבי עבודת כוכבים דכתיב מן הדרך, אפילו מקצת דרך, וחייב בקיום מקצת ובין על כל הגוף, אבל בשאר מצוות אינו חייב אלא בביטול כל הגוף. ויש לומר דהתם כתיב ללכת בה, ותניא בספרי: ולא העושה במקצת ומשייר מקצת מיעוט בהדי קיום מקצת. להכי בעבודת כוכבים דגלי קרא, חייב אפילו במקצת הגוף. וגם בביטול כל הגוף חייב, דלא גרע משאר מצוות. ואי לאו מיעוט דשאר מצוות והוי כתיב סתמא, היה חייב נמי בשאר מצוות בכל ענין. והכי נמי הכא, ולהכי כתיב הכא דבר למעוטי כל הגוף. וליכא למימר אפכא, דדבר כולו דבר משמע, דתניא בתורת כהנים: כתיב הכא מכל מצוות ה', וכתיב במשיח מכל מצוות ה'. ואי לא דמיחייב אלא בעוקר כל הגוף, לא משכחת במצוות האמורות אלא בתו מאנוסתו, ואם חמותו, ואם חמיו, דבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו. הועתק מפירוש רבינו שמחה זכרונו לברכה:
Tosafot on Horayot 4a:9:1.english: Read into it as "venelam middavar": For the mem of "venelam" applies to both here and there; and it is said in the Yerushalmi that some say we subtract and expound from the beginning of a section to its end, and others say even in the middle of a section: "And you shall pour oil on it," "you poured oil of the meal offering," to teach that all meal offerings require pouring. Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Meir asked: What is different that here we expound "venelam middavar," and regarding testimony, "a matter shall be established" (Deuteronomy 19:15), everyone expounds "a matter" and not "half a matter"? And one can say that certainly "matter" implies the entire thing, but here, from the context of the verse: since it is written "one of all the *mitzvot* of the Lord," which implies an entire *mitzva*, for what *halakha* did it write "matter"? Rather, it must be to expound "venelam middavar," even one detail of the *mitzvot*. And similarly in all places, we subtract and add and expound because of the difficulty of the verse, for it is difficult and stands on its own. Like that of gold, where it should have been written "and a fifth he shall add to it," just as it is written regarding tithes. And in the chapter "Yesh Nochalin," it should have been written "his wife shall inherit the inheritance," and when the verse is written, one needs to resolve the verse by subtraction and addition. A wonder: From where do we know that the verse comes to obligate only for sustaining a portion and nullifying a portion? Perhaps the verse comes even to obligate in this, and all the more so in abolishing the entire essence, as it says in the chapter "HaNikhnakin" regarding idol worship, that it is written "from the way," even part of the way, and one is liable for sustaining a portion and for the entire essence, but for other *mitzvot* one is only liable for abolishing the entire essence. And one can say that there it is written "to walk in it," and it is taught in the Sifrei: "and not one who does partially and leaves partially" — a limitation alongside sustaining a portion. Therefore, regarding idol worship, where the verse reveals, one is liable even for part of the essence. And also for abolishing the entire essence, one is liable, for it is no less than other *mitzvot*. And if not for the limitation of other *mitzvot* and it was written generally, one would also be liable for other *mitzvot* in every case. And so too here, and therefore it is written here "matter" to exclude the entire essence. And one cannot say the opposite, that "matter" implies the entire thing, for it is taught in Torat Kohanim: Here it is written "of all the *mitzvot* of the Lord," and it is written regarding the Anointed Priest "of all the *mitzvot* of the Lord." And if one is only liable for abolishing the entire essence, you would not find among the aforementioned *mitzvot* except for his daughter from a raped woman, and if his mother-in-law, and if his father-in-law — a matter about which the Sadducees do not agree. Copied from the commentary of our Rabbi Simcha, may his memory be a blessing:
